calls.prompt:
You are an experienced clinician auditing a clinical note for statements that the consultation does not support. Below is the note. List every clinical claim it makes, so each can later be checked against the consultation.

<note>
(the above consultation reason doesn't correlate with the patient's presentation)
Remote consultation- video lost early on, continued audio-only with pt's agreement, so no examination performed. Pt gave age 32; DOB not obtained.
Hx: pt describes 'weird' episodic symptoms that he cannot explain himself, which prompted him to seek help- episodes of unilateral right hand/arm loss of feeling and pins and needles (pins and needles confined to the hand), with some arm and leg weakness (side of leg not specified) and gait disturbance noticed by his colleague lasting 3-4 days, duration uncertain- initially agreed with 'about a month', then estimated 1.5-2 months himself
occurring with increasing frequency- initially once a week to once a month, now a couple of times a day
also generally tired, weak and nauseated over this period; in the last couple of days unable to hold his coffee cup and slightly harder to drink, during episodes only
symptoms not present now, and normally fit and well between episodes
no dysphagia currently, though describes a sensation of something in his throat during episodes; no dysphasia; no visual symptoms during episodes (wears glasses)
no Pmhx of CVA/TIA
Father had an operation to the side of his neck to reduce stroke risk
Non smoker, normal diabetes/ cholesterol/ BP checks when screened after his father's operation
PMHx: no other illnesses; wider FH not asked about
Allergies: penicillin (only)
DH PT IS TAKING Aspirin 75mg OD on his own accord, self-started after his father's operation on the basis of something he read online in the belief it reduces the risk of stroke and heart attack, never previously discussed with a GP- no change made today
SH: pt is a medical doctor, plastic surgeon, lives with wife; no ideas or concerns of his own as to the cause
Imp: confirmed diagnosis of TIAs, despite young age
Plan: needs to be seen urgently in TIA clinic- will send referral now. Clinic expected to call within 1-2 days; today is Wednesday, ie seen by Thurs/Fri. Carotid USS +/- brain imaging anticipated at clinic- nothing arranged or performed today. PALS no and TIA clinic no to be left in these consultation notes so pt can chase the appointment- advised he can ring the clinic himself later today (after waiting an hour or two) or tomorrow am to confirm he is in the system and booked in, and to contact us again if any delay or he is not called
If any prolonged symptoms occur- to attend A/E asap; not an immediate emergency today
</note>

A claim is one checkable clinical statement: a symptom or its absence, a history item, an examination finding, a test result, a diagnosis or assessment, a medication and its dose, a plan item, advice or a follow-up arrangement. Keep each claim's qualifiers (side, dose, frequency, timing, negation, uncertainty) with it. Split a sentence that makes several independent statements; do not split one statement into fragments. Skip headings, the patient's name, and pure formatting.

For each claim give "claim" (a short plain statement) and "quote": the passage of the note that makes it, copied word for word (at most 40 words).

Reply with only this JSON object, no other text:
